main_topics.reason: The user opened with severe nausea after weekly methotrexate and the whole conversation worked on reducing it.
The user asked whether they could quit and later asked whether to keep taking it until the appointment.
The user asked which day to take folic acid and admitted sometimes taking it on the methotrexate day, over several turns.
The user asked how much difference the injection makes and said they were scared of self-injecting.
The user asked whether anti-nausea medicine is safe with methotrexate after learning it was an option.
The user asked what to say to the doctor so as not to forget and planned to write down the script.
The user briefly said they were a little scared of injecting themselves.
The user mentioned once that their hands are much better on methotrexate, as background for keeping it.

output.summary: A user with rheumatoid arthritis wanted to quit methotrexate because of severe weekly nausea. The bot explained options (folic acid timing, dose splitting, anti-nausea medicine, injection), advised not to stop on their own, gave warning signs needing earlier medical contact, and helped draft a note for the doctor. The user said they felt much better and planned to make changes that weekend.
